mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the investor's jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, the document must be notarized by a local notary and then apostilled by the competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State or Ministry of Foreign Affairs). If the jurisdiction is not a member, the document must be notarized and then legalized by the Chinese consulate in that jurisdiction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocol: All beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must undergo enhanced due diligence screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Chinese Ministry of Public Security's list of politically exposed persons (PEPs). The screening must cover all nationalities and jurisdictions, including cross-referencing with the World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms. For PEPs, a risk-based approach is applied: high-risk PEPs require senior management approval and enhanced monitoring. The screening must be conducted at onboarding and continuously updated on a real-time basis using automated compliance software. Any positive hit triggers immediate suspension of the formation process and a mandatory report to the PBOC and SAMR within 24 hours. The protocol also includes adverse media screening and verification of source of funds for the initial capital contribution.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration System (NENRS) under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese name must be in simplified Chinese characters. An English name is optional but must be consistent with the Chinese name. The name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + trade name + industry characteristics + legal form (e.g., 'Shanghai [Trade Name] Technology Co., Ltd.'). For foreign trade names, phonetic transliteration is permitted, but the transliteration must be approved by SAMR. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法) Articles 6, 129, 154, 161-162, 192, 208 and 387; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例) Articles 7-8 and the Enforcement Rules of the Foreign Investment Act; Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area if the ultimate investor is a mainland Chinese person or entity; MOEA Company Registration and Fee Charging Standards
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), with local municipal commercial offices having jurisdiction over the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Incorporation (Company Establishment Registration Application) submitted under Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act, resulting in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Taiwan Company Act for a limited liability WFOE; the paid-up capital must nevertheless be sufficient for the stated business scope as reviewed by the Investment Commission. Foreign share capital must be remitted from abroad into a temporary Taiwan bank account in the name of the proposed company and verified by a Taiwan certified public accountant. No blocked escrow account is required by statute, but the capital must remain in the company account for operating purposes and may not be returned to the investor before lawful distribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [•] TAIWAN LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY. I, the undersigned, being all the initial directors of [•] Taiwan Limited Liability Company (the 'Company'), do hereby convene the first board meeting by unanimous written consent and adopt the following resolutions. WHEREAS the Company was organized to develop, license, distribute and operate AI avatar video generation software and related SaaS services under ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; WHEREAS the Company has received investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, and the foreign shareholder has committed to subscribe for the entire initial issued share capital; WHEREAS the Company must adopt its registered office, open bank accounts, appoint statutory officers and authorize the issuance of share capital in accordance with the Taiwan Company Act; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED. 1. Share Capital Subscription, Allotment and Issuance. The Board approves the subscription of the Company's authorized capital of NT$[•], divided into [•] ordinary shares with par value NT$[•] per share. The paid-in capital of NT$[•] has been subscribed by the sole foreign shareholder and deposited into a temporary capital account in the name of the Company at [Bank], Taiwan branch. The Board confirms that the subscriptions are fully paid, that no share consideration remains outstanding, and that no shares are issued at a discount or for prohibited non-cash consideration. The Board authorizes the Chairman to instruct the certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report as required by Article 387 of the Taiwan Company Act. 2. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is hereby adopted at [street address, district, city, Taiwan], which shall also be the tax and mailing address. The Company Secretary is directed to file the registered office with the Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA, to display the company identification plate and to maintain the statutory books at that address. 3. Banking Authorization. The Board approves [Bank], Taiwan branch, as the principal banker of the Company. The Chairman, General Manager and Chief Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized to open operating, payroll, foreign currency and treasury accounts for the Company. All cheques, wire instructions, acceptances and payment orders above NT$[•] must be signed by two authorized signatories, one of whom shall be the Chairman or General Manager. The banker is authorized to act on signed instruments consistent with this resolution. 4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [Name] is appointed Chairman and statutory representative; [Name] is appointed Director; [Name] is appointed General Manager; [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary. Each officer accepts office and shall perform duties with fiduciary care under Articles 23 and 192 of the Taiwan Company Act. 5. Company Seal and Corporate Instruments. The Chairman is authorized to procure a common corporate seal and a finance seal, and to execute the incorporation application, tax registrations, office lease, employment agreements, software license agreements and merchant account applications with Stripe and Paddle. 6. General Administrative Authorization. All officers and registered agents identified by the Chairman are authorized to make all filings, pay all statutory fees, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and take all lawful steps to commence the Company's AI avatar video generation business. The resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until amended or revoked by the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Acquire foreign investment approval and capital remittance clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.) - online foreign investment service portal and physical counter at the MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Foreign Investment Application to the Investment Commission through the online portal. The application must identify the ultimate investor, the proposed Taiwan WFOE name, the proposed paid-up share capital, the ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210 business scope for AI avatar video generation and SaaS delivery, and the intended payment rail providers. The Commission will screen the negative-list restrictions, national security concerns, capital source and business plan. If the beneficial owner is a mainland Chinese entity or individual, the filing must be routed through the Mainland Investment Review desk under the Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, and only permitted business activities may be approved. After approval, the investor must remit the subscribed capital into a temporary Taiwan bank account in the name of the Company, and the remittance record must be retained for CPA capital verification.
required_dossiers: Completed foreign investment application form
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and board resolution, notarized or authenticated as applicable
Business plan for AI avatar video generation software and SaaS operations
Draft Articles of Incorporation of the Taiwan WFOE
Power of attorney appointing a Taiwan registered agent
Proof of investor financial standing or audited financial statements
Capital remittance projection and proposed bank in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency letter or suspends the application, the investor must respond with corrected or supplemental documents within the stated cure period, usually 30 days. If the application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to MOEA within 30 days of written notice, or submit a revised application with an adjusted business scope and capital structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and confirm business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA - MOEA Company Registration Information System (online company name reservation window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the MOEA Company Registration Information System and file a company name and business scope pre-approval application. The applicant must provide the Chinese company name, the English company name, the proposed business scope text describing AI avatar video generation software development, licensing and system integration, and the approved foreign investment reference number. MOEA will screen for identical or confusingly similar names with existing registered companies and reserved names. The pre-approved name remains valid for six months and may be extended once. The business scope must match the investment approval letter and the future Articles of Incorporation. If the Company intends to use an English name for Stripe and Paddle, the English name should be stated as the official registered English company name, while the Chinese name is filed with MOEA for statutory purposes.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation application form
Foreign investment approval letter
Proposed Chinese and English company names
Proposed business scope text for AI avatar video generation software
Applicant identification or power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of conflict or confusing similarity, the applicant should select a new distinctive name and resubmit the reservation application. If the business scope is rejected, the applicant should amend the description to align with Taiwan's permitted software service categories and, if necessary, obtain an updated foreign investment approval letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles of Incorporation, remit capital and obtain CPA capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-certified public accountant registered under the Financial Supervisory Commission; founding shareholder and initial directors acting by corporate action
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the name reservation and investment approval are obtained, the founding shareholder executes the Articles of Incorporation and the initial directors adopt the first board resolution. The foreign shareholder must remit the paid-up capital from its home country to a temporary bank account in Taiwan held under the proposed company name. The remittance advice, SWIFT message and bank statement must be delivered to a Taiwan certified public accountant. The CPA will assess whether the contribution is monetary, fully paid and lawfully remitted, and will issue a capital verification report stating the paid-up capital amount, shareholder identities and proof of remittance. The Articles must include the company name, business scope, registered address, share structure, internal governance and liquidation clauses. The subscription list must be signed by the sole shareholder and countersigned by the chairman.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Foreign investment approval letter and name reservation letter
Capital remittance evidence via SWIFT MT103 or bank transfer advice
Bank statement from temporary Taiwan account in the proposed company name
CPA capital verification report
Signed subscription list and first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA questions the source of funds, currency mismatch or remittance timing, the investor must obtain a corrected SWIFT or bank confirmation from the remitting bank, provide source-of-funds evidence, or make a supplemental remittance. The capital verification defect must be fully cured before the incorporation application is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit incorporation application and obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA, or the municipal commercial office with jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through MOEA Company Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official Application for Company Incorporation with the Department of Commercial Affairs or the municipal commercial office with jurisdiction over the registered office. The application package must include the name reservation letter, investment approval letter, Articles of Incorporation, CPA capital verification report, subscription list, director and chairman appointment consents, registered office lease or landlord consent, and foreign shareholder identification. The registration officer will verify the statutory particulars and issue a Certificate of Incorporation under Article 6 of the Taiwan Company Act. If integrated local filing is available, the system will automatically forward tax registration data to the National Taxation Bureau. The applicant should pay the official filing fee at the electronic counter and retain the fee receipt. The Company must confirm that no share is issued below par and that the paid-in capital is deposited and available.
required_dossiers: Application for Company Incorporation
Name reservation letter
Foreign investment approval letter
Articles of Incorporation signed by all shareholders
CPA capital verification report
Signed subscription list
Director and chairman appointment consents
Certificate of registered office address and landlord consent
Foreign shareholder identification and corporate authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a correction notice, the applicant must submit the missing or corrected documents within 15 days. If the application is rejected, the applicant may file a new application with clarifications or lodge an administrative appeal to MOEA within 30 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, labor, and digital-service post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance; local municipal fire and occupational safety authorities for office premises only
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, the Company must file for value-added and business tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau, applying for a Taiwan Uniform Invoice Certificate and tax withholding registration. The Company must enroll directors and employees in Labor Insurance, National Health Insurance and Labor Pension programs through the Bureau of Labor Insurance. For a pure digital ISIC 6201 software business, no industrial operating license is required; however, if physical office space is leased, the local municipality will require a fire safety inspection certificate for the premises and compliance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act. The Company should also complete merchant onboarding for Stripe and Paddle by submitting the certificate of incorporation, tax clearance evidence and AML/KYC corporate documents for the Low_Risk_Standard banking risk tier.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Foreign investment approval letter
Tax registration application form
Lease agreement for registered office
Uniform Invoice Certificate application
Director and officer identification documents
Labor insurance and health insurance enrollment forms
AML/KYC corporate packet for Stripe and Paddle
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau returns the registration, the Company must cure identified matters such as missing address proof or mismatched business scope and re-file within 30 days. If labor enrollment is queried, the Company must provide employment records and amended contracts. Any tax assessment or registration denial may be appealed to the Ministry of Finance within 30 days of written notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 is a pure software service activity involving AI avatar video generation, and no industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing licensing authority applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (R.O.C.) (formerly the Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - AI avatar video generation software is a non-manufacturing, non-physical digital service, and does not constitute a development activity under Article 4 of the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no EIA report, initial environmental examination or environmental registration certificate is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the software activity generates no wastewater, waste gas, volatile organic compound or hazardous waste streams. Office occupancy must comply with general waste disposal under the Waste Disposal Act, but no quantitative industrial discharge or emissions permit limits attach to pure software operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for an industrial Civil Defense fire permit or structural load approval. If the Company occupies a physical office, the lessor must supply a current fire safety inspection certificate under the Taiwan Fire Services Act, and the Company must maintain workplace safety, emergency evacuation procedures and occupational health management in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (Taiwan); registration and tax administration are executed by the regional National Taxation Bureaus (e.g., National Taxation Bureau of Taipei). The official online electronic portal is the 'Integrated Tax Filing and Registration System' operated by the National Taxation Bureau, accessible at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the inbound foreign-owned Taiwan limited liability company (WFOE): (1) file for company incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain the company registration certificate; (2) within 15 days of incorporation, apply for business tax (VAT) registration at the local National Taxation Bureau by submitting the statutory Tax Registration Application Form, the company registration certificate, the articles of incorporation, the list of shareholders, the responsible person's identification (passport/ID), and the physical business premises evidence (lease agreement or title deed); (3) undergo the Bureau's premises inspection; (4) receive the Tax Registration Number (unified business number) and the authoritative Uniform Invoice seal. For a foreign non-resident entity without a permanent establishment that sells electronic services to Taiwan consumers, the non-resident must: (a) appoint a local tax agent; (b) register online through the National Taxation Bureau's 'Cross-Border Electronic Services Tax Registration' portal using the home-country registration certificate, the agent's authorization, and a description of the electronic services; (c) obtain a Business Tax Registration Number for the account; and (d) begin charging Taiwan business tax at the statutory rate on transactions with Taiwan individuals, filing bimonthly returns through the tax agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None – Taiwan does not offer a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election for corporate entities; all companies are taxed at entity level under the Income Tax Act, and no pass-through treatment is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For domestic VAT-registered enterprises, mandatory registration is triggered when average monthly sales exceed TWD 200,000 (annual equivalent TWD 2,400,000); for foreign non-resident electronic services suppliers, registration is mandatory when annual Taiwan turnover exceeds TWD 480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered businesses must issue 'Uniform Invoices' for all sales. The Ministry of Finance mandates electronic invoices (e-invoices) for most taxpayers, requiring issuance through the MOF e-Invoice Integrated Platform or an approved E-Invoice Turnkey service provider. E-invoice data must be transmitted to the platform via API/Turnkey within 48 hours of issuance (real-time for cloud invoices), and each e-invoice must carry a tax verification QR code. Foreign digital service providers must issue e-invoices to Taiwan consumers and upload the data through the same platform, which performs real-time anti-fraud checks and assigns a unique invoice number and QR stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, zero rating applies to exported goods and services. For the supply of AI avatar video generation SaaS, zero rating is available when (1) the service is used or consumed outside Taiwan, (2) the service is not deemed to be rendered within Taiwan for a Taiwan customer, and (3) the consideration is received in foreign currency. The exporter must substantiate that the customer is a non-resident and that the service was delivered electronically to a location outside Taiwan, with the transaction recorded as an export sale for business tax purposes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export service contract or purchase order evidencing the foreign buyer and the scope of the digital service
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank credit advice showing receipt of the foreign-currency consideration from outside Taiwan

Electronic service delivery records (e.g., server logs with non-Taiwan IP geolocation, customer account verification, or user acceptance certificate) demonstrating that the service is used outside Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau conducts document reviews and audits of zero-rated export claims. If the zero rating is disallowed due to insufficient or inconsistent documentation, the unpaid business tax at 5% is assessed together with interest, and a penalty of 1x to 1.5x the underpaid tax is imposed. For fraudulent claims, including counterfeit FIRCs, fictitious export contracts, or misrepresentation of the place of use, the penalty increases to 1x to 5x of the tax evaded, and criminal liability may arise under the Tax Evasion and Punishment Act if the evaded amount exceeds TWD 50,000. Retrospective clawbacks extend up to seven years for fraud and five years for ordinary deficiencies.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC), with the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) as co-regulator for banking and the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Investment Commission for inbound foreign/mainland investment admission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) is fully legal tender in Taiwan but is not an international reserve currency; Taiwan runs a managed floating exchange-rate system under the CBC with TWD/USD and TWD/CNY rates determined in the interbank market and smoothed by the central bank. For current-account flows, Taiwan is broadly convertible: software licensing, SaaS subscription fees, royalty payments, management charges, freight income and profit remittances from a foreign-invested enterprise can be converted into TWD or retained in designated foreign-currency deposit accounts once the underlying contract, invoices, customs declaration or audited financial statement and tax clearance are presented. There is no blanket current-account conversion ceiling, but the CBC receives electronic Exchange Settlement Reports for statistical, macro-prudential and AML purposes. Capital-account flows are far less free: inbound equity injection, shareholder loans, the acquisition of existing shares, local direct investment and outward investment by Taiwan entities must be approved by the MOEA Investment Commission (financial sectors under FSC) and then settled through an authorized FX bank. Profit remittance to a mainland Chinese parent is treated as a regulated remittance: it requires an audited Taiwan WFOE balance sheet, certified compliance with undistributed retained earnings tax under the Income Tax Act, original foreign-investment admission approval, and a tax payment/tax clearance certificate before the bank files the outward remittance report. The practical hurdle is documentary, not quantitative: no tariff or remittance cap exists for legitimate dividends, but every payment must be reconciled to approved share capital, audited earnings and paid corporate income tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must repatriate the full foreign-currency invoice value to a Taiwan-licensed bank within 180 calendar days from the export customs declaration date for goods; for service exports, the 180-day clock runs from the service completion date or invoice date and is supported by the service contract and settlement invoice. The bank must file the Foreign Exchange Settlement Report through the CBC reporting system and retain the Customs Export Declaration, marine/AWB waybill, commercial invoice and payment evidence. There is no mandatory conversion percentage: 0% of export proceeds must be converted into TWD, and the exporter may keep 100% in a Foreign-Currency Deposit Account or convert any portion at market rate. Any overdue collection, extended open account, D/A, D/P, consignment or barter arrangement must be approved in advance by the designated bank and reported to the CBC; the exporter should maintain credit insurance, collection agency correspondence or buyer default evidence in the event of delay.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is restricted to pure payment-acquiring rails; offshore EMIs are not permitted to operate as deposit-taking banks for a Taiwan WFOE. Stripe and Paddle are valid as card/payment aggregator or merchant-of-record rails for collecting AI avatar video SaaS revenue, but neither is licensed by the FSC to maintain TWD corporate accounts, hold statutory capital in escrow, or process foreign-exchange settlement on behalf of the entity. The funds from Stripe/Paddle must be settled, usually in USD or TWD, directly into the WFOE's Taiwan-licensed bank account through authorized acquiring or payout rails; all statutory capital and capital verification must flow through a Tier-1 domestic bank via SWIFT, not through Wise, Airwallex, Stripe Treasury or Paddle Treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch appearance is generally mandatory for the statutory director/responsible person and at least one authorized signatory at the time of Taiwan corporate account opening. Most banks do not offer pure online onboarding to a non-Taiwan-controlled WFOE. Remote consular proxy opening is possible only on an exceptional, relationship-manager-approved basis, where the director executes a notarized power of attorney that is submitted to MOEA/consular legalization, accompanied by live recorded video KYC and a subsequent in-branch verification within a short window. Where the ultimate investor is a mainland China entity, enhanced due diligence applies and the bank may insist on the mainland UBO appearing in-person at the Taiwan branch or at a designated correspondent office before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a mainland China individual/company, creating an enhanced cross-strait AML, sanctions and anti-economic-espionage review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO register and full ownership chain; passport/business license copies for all intermediate shareholders; MOEA Investment Commission approval letter for mainland investment in Taiwan; source-of-wealth report; audited financial statements for the previous three years; bank reference letters from the Chinese parent's domestic bank; OFAC/UN/EU/UK sanctions, FATF high-risk jurisdiction and denial-list screening reports; and a written explanation of the business purpose for Taiwan establishment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI avatar video SaaS revenue via Stripe and Paddle creates high-volume, low-ticket digital collections from anonymous global end-users, raising third-party money-laundering and export-control concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed merchant service agreements with Stripe and Paddle; merchant KYC and underwriting summaries; transaction monitoring configuration logs; IP address geoblocking proof excluding sanctioned territories; automated sanctions/PEP name screening logs; chargeback and refund policies; end-user license terms and use restrictions for AI avatar generation; export-control classification memo for ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 software; and evidence that settled proceeds are swept to Taiwan WFOE bank accounts only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin capitalization and lack of physical Taiwan operational substance suggest the WFOE may be a shell used for invoice parking, treaty abuse or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease and utility bills; payroll and Taiwan labor insurance records for local staff if any; Taiwan corporate income tax, VAT and withholding tax returns; board resolutions and minutes of actual Taiwan board meetings; transfer-pricing documentation for intercompany software licensing and support fees; bank statements showing Taiwan-local operating expenditure; and a substance roadmap showing local data hosting, customer support or AI model parameterization activities in Taiwan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity capital arrives from a related Chinese entity or from a third-party payment channel rather than an approved foreign investor account, violating FX and capital verification rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Inbound SWIFT MT103 message with the remitter name matching the approved MOEA investor; CBC-compliant FDI purpose code indicating equity subscription; certified copy of the board resolution authorizing share issuance; CPA-issued capital verification report; bank's Foreign Exchange Settlement Report; approval letter of foreign/mainland investment; shareholder loan agreements if intercompany debt is injected; banker's draft for the injection; and a source-of-funds certificate from the originating bank showing no cash or crypto layering.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The parent must route all FDI equity capital by SWIFT MT103 from its approved corporate bank in mainland China to the Taiwan WFOE's designated TWD/FCD account at Bank of Taiwan, Mega, or CTBC, using a CBC-compliant purpose code that clearly identifies direct investment/equity subscription rather than trade. The Taiwan receiving bank will not credit funds to operational accounts until it has verified the MOEA/FSC investment approval, share subscription resolution, source-of-funds evidence and the identity of the remitter. After receipt, an appointed Taiwan CPA must issue a capital verification report, and the bank files the Foreign Exchange Settlement Report. Only after those documents are complete may the WFOE draw funds down for SaaS platform build-out, local operations and acquisition of AI compute or cloud services.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For software license fees, royalties, intercompany support fees and dividend remittances, use direct SWIFT MT103 international wire transfers through the Taiwan clearing network, with the underlying contract, tax clearance and CBC purpose code attached. For bundled hardware/software sales, the WFOE may use a Commercial Letter of Credit governed by UCP 600 or Documentary Collections under URC 522 for export shipments of any physical edge devices or server components; digital-only SaaS subscriptions are settled via the Stripe/Paddle merchant acquirer and swept to the Taiwan bank account. All outbound trade disbursements must be made from the WFOE's own account to the counterparty's account, not via cash or third-party netting, and must be reported through the authorized FX bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright TWD/USD and TWD/CNY forward contracts through CBC-designated domestic FX banks, supported by documentary evidence of the underlying subscription revenue, intercompany royalty stream or approved inward capital transaction; no speculative rollover without genuine exposure.
Foreign exchange swaps (TWD/USD) for symmetric cash-flow timing on an approved capital injection and a later dividend payout, with the notional capped by the approved underlying transaction.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) between USD, TWD and CNY to hedge a shareholder loan or external borrowing, subject to FSC recognition of the borrower as an eligible corporation and the swap's direct linkage to the actual loan principal and interest obligations.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on TWD are available only to offshore counterparties and are effectively prohibited for a domestic Taiwan WFOE with TWD revenue; the entity should instead rely on deliverable forwards, FX swaps and CCIRS, and any NDF booking by an offshore affiliate must remain outside the Taiwan-regulated banking perimeter and must not affect local treasury settlements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Business Operation Report for Foreign-Invested WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEIC), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March for a calendar-year WFOE; within three months after the close of the fiscal year unless an extension is approved in writing by the Investment Commission before the original due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$50,000 (approximately USD 1,620); continued non-compliance after a 30-day correction order may lead to revocation of foreign investment approval, suspension of dividend/capital remittance, and administrative strike-off of the foreign investor registration if the report is not filed for two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Approval of Audited Financial Statements, Business Report, and Earnings Appropriation; Minutes Retention and Filing if Director Election or Articles Amendment Occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Office and the local municipal competent authority where the WFOE is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be held on or before 30 June, i.e., within six months after fiscal year-end; meeting minutes must be submitted for registration within 15 days of the meeting only if directors are elected or the Articles of Association are amended; otherwise the minutes are kept at the registered office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 (approximately USD 320 to USD 1,620) for non-compliant minute keeping or refusal to permit inspection; failure to convene the AGM by 30 June may result in fines against company officers and, upon continued default for six months, administrative dissolution/strike-off under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Corporate Income Tax Settlement Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (local tax administration having jurisdiction over the WFOE registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed between 1 May and 31 May for a calendar-year company; extension to 30 June is available when the return is e-filed and prepared by a licensed tax agent or certified public accountant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing adds 2% of the delinquent tax amount for each two-month period or part thereof, up to a maximum of 9%, plus default interest from the original due date at the one-year postal savings fixed deposit rate; unpaid tax after a 30-day demand may trigger tax liens and compulsory collection; fraudulent understatement may expose the company to penalties of up to three times the tax underpaid and criminal liability for responsible officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (local tax administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six returns per fiscal year; each must be filed on or before the 15th day after the end of the two-month period, i.e., by 15 January, 15 March, 15 May, 15 July, 15 September, and 15 November for calendar-year filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of NT$1,500 (approximately USD 50) plus a late-payment surcharge of 2% of the tax due for each month or fraction thereof, capped at 20%; repeated non-filing may lead to compulsory suspension of business operations and administrative strike-off of the VAT registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation and Maintenance of Statutory Corporate Registers and Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office in Taiwan; available for inspection by MOEA, the Investment Commission, and designated anti-money-laundering authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing maintenance obligation; registers must be updated within 15 days of any qualifying change and must be confirmed as accurate by a board/AGM resolution at the annual shareholders meeting no later than 30 June of each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance attracts a fine of NT$10,000 to NT$100,000 (approximately USD 320 to USD 3,240), plus a continuing daily fine while the default persists; failure to maintain UBO data may be treated as anti-money-laundering non-compliance and, after repeated correction orders, may culminate in administrative dissolution/strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit by a licensed Taiwanese CPA is mandatory if any of the following quantitative thresholds is exceeded at the latest fiscal year-end: (i) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000); (ii) annual operating turnover exceeds NT$100,000,000 (approximately USD 3,300,000); (iii) total balance-sheet assets exceed NT$100,000,000 (approximately USD 3,300,000); or (iv) average headcount exceeds 100 employees. A WFOE may also be required to file audited financial statements where the Investment Commission imposes an audit condition in the foreign investment approval, or where the entity operates in a regulated financial, insurance, or electronic-payment-related activity subject to Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) oversight.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS, being International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission; non-public WFOEs may prepare statutory financial statements using the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Guidelines (SME-oriented framework), but audited statutory financial statements must be presented in accordance with Taiwan-IFRS or ROC GAAP and accompanied by a CPA opinion issued under Taiwan Statements on Auditing Standards (TSAS).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan's Company Act and anti-money-laundering regime require the WFOE to maintain at its registered office a current register of shareholders, directors, managers, and ultimate beneficial owners. Any transfer of shares or change in ownership that alters direct or indirect beneficial ownership of 25% or more must be recorded in the register within 30 days of the transaction and, where the corporate registration file must change, notified to MOEA. At each annual shareholders meeting, the board must confirm that the register is accurate, incorporate all shareholding transfers that occurred during the preceding year, and ensure the register and underlying records are accessible for inspection by MOEA, the Investment Commission, and AML authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 1,800 per annum for a professional registered office and corporate agent in Taiwan, including statutory address services, UBO register maintenance, and ministerial notice handling.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 12,000 per annum for a non-public WFOE engaged in low-risk AI avatar video generation SaaS operations, assuming moderate transaction volume and no consolidated group reporting; fees increase for multi-entity consolidation, cross-border financing structures, IFRS conversion complexities, or FSC-regulated payment rails.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax of 20% with the following reductions: (i) 12% Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) floor on preferential items; (ii) R&D investment tax credit of up to 15% of qualifying AI-software R&D expenditure under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, limited to 30% of computed tax payable; (iii) full exemption for taxable income not exceeding NT$120,000 with phased tapering; (iv) 5% retained-earnings tax on undistributed profit that is not distributed within 12 months, effectively mandating full distribution to the Chinese parent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (营利事业所得税结算申报书, Form No. 15) together with balance sheet, income statement, and statutory schedules; e-filed via the Ministry of Finance electronic filing portal (财政部电子申报缴税服务网) and administered by the National Taxation Bureau.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return with a provisional (tentative) income tax payment filed 1-30 September of the current year based on the prior-year tax; no separate quarterly corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The final settlement return must be filed by the last day of the fifth month following the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, the deadline is 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from AI avatar video generation SaaS subscriptions, per-generation usage fees, and software licensing receipts recognized under IFRS 15.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwanese WFOE is a resident filer; report only revenue attributed to Taiwan operations and separately disclose any related-party intercompany revenue with the Chinese parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 31 – 营业费用含研究发展费用
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: developer payroll, GPU cloud hosting, data center costs, marketing, and R&D expenses claimed for the R&D tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-arm's-length management fees, IP royalties, or service charges paid to the PRC parent must be excluded unless supported by transfer pricing documentation and beneficial-ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income after transfer pricing adjustments, statutory exemptions, and loss carryforward deductions not exceeding 10 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement only at the WHT stage; the treaty does not reduce Taiwan-resident WFOE taxable income directly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule – 关系人交易汇总表 (Related-Party Transaction Summary Table)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory annual disclosure of transactions with related parties: goods, services, intangible property licensing, royalty, financing, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Itemize all transactions with the Chinese shareholder/affiliates and attach the Local File when the NT$50 million service/intangibles threshold is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule – 投资抵减税额明细表 (Investment Tax Credit Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the R&D tax credit and AMT worksheet; credits are elective and generally carry forward up to 4 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify eligibility and board authorization before claiming; credits are subject to audit by the National Taxation Bureau.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing accrues a surcharge of 1% of tax payable per month or fraction thereof, capped at 20%; non-filing after a rectification notice accrues 3% per month capped at 30%; under-reported taxable income attracts a penalty of 2x-3x of the evaded tax and, for intentional concealment, up to 5x; unpaid tax bears interest at the one-year postal deposit rate; responsible persons are subject to exit restriction when arrears exceed NT$1 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Cross-Strait Tax Agreement (signed 25 August 2015, effective 1 January 2016) reduces dividend withholding tax to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the WFOE's capital, and to 10% in all other cases. Relief protocol: (1) the PRC parent must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (税收居民证明) from the State Taxation Administration; (2) the Taiwan WFOE as withholding agent files the treaty-relief application form (租税协定减免所得税申请表) with the local National Taxation Bureau, attaching the TRC, shareholding registry extract, and beneficial-ownership statement; (3) upon approval, withholding is applied at the treaty rate; the application may be made retrospectively for dividends within the same calendar year and requires annual renewal.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 20% withholding on royalties paid to a non-resident and 20% withholding on interest paid to a non-resident corporate lender. Under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement the rates are treaty-capped at 7% for royalties and 7% for interest, subject to beneficial-ownership, TRC, and substance conditions; bank-to-enterprise interest may qualify for the reduced rate only with complete documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (移转订价报告) is mandatory where annual related-party transactions exceed NT$200 million for goods or NT$50 million for services and intangible property licensing/transfers; the Related-Party Transaction Summary Table is required for all filers; Master File is required where consolidated group turnover reaches NT$30 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the UAE sense, but the tax administration enforces equivalent substance tests via the Place of Effective Management (PEM) doctrine, the GAAR under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act, and the cross-strait anti-avoidance coordination mechanism. A Taiwan WFOE must demonstrate real local board decision-making, physical R&D staff, source-code and server control in Taiwan, genuine risk assumption, and arm's-length intercompany agreements; otherwise profits are reallocated to the PRC parent or the entity is recharacterized as a tax-transparent shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Fraudulent Returns and False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating AI avatar SaaS subscription revenue received via Stripe/Paddle, fabricating developer labor costs, or using counterfeit electronic invoices (不实发票) to inflate deductible expenses and reduce Taiwan taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of evaded tax plus a 2x-3x penalty (up to 5x for deliberate concealment) under Articles 108 and 110 of the Income Tax Act; criminal prosecution under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act (2021 amendment) carrying imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fines up to NT$5 million; administrative delisting and adverse filing status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person who signs the false return is jointly prosecuted; the National Taxation Bureau may impose an exit restriction (限制出境) where delinquent tax exceeds NT$1 million; civil restitution is enforceable against personal assets of directing officers; cross-strait tax information exchange permits the PRC tax authority to support collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties or inflated management fees to the PRC parent for AI avatar core IP while the Taiwan WFOE retains all operational substance, such that Taiwan reports negligible profit despite hosting the platform and serving customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act and the Transfer Pricing Examination Standards: upward adjustment of taxable income, 20% tax on the additional assessment, 5% retained-earnings tax on undeclared surplus, 20% WHT recapture on recharacterized royalties or fees, plus daily interest and penalties up to 3x of the adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers are jointly answerable for the unpaid withholding tax and assessed penalties; exit restrictions apply for sustained non-payment; deliberate TP fraud triggers criminal liability and personal seizure; the PRC parent may be treated as the substantive taxpayer under the PEM doctrine.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan WFOE operates as a paper entity: mailbox office only, no local employees, no control over the AI source code or platform servers, no local board meetings, and all management decisions made in Shenzhen or Hangzhou with fund flows routed through the parent treasury.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization under Article 43-1 of the Income Tax Act and the PEM rule: the entire profit is reattributed to the PRC parent or treated as a Taiwan permanent establishment of the parent; assessment of 20% corporate tax on recharacterized profit, 21% dividend WHT recapture, denial of loss deductions, and penalties for false reporting; possible forced dissolution for non-operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person is liable for restitution of the recharacterized profit; travel bans under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act; personal fraud exposure in egregious cases; cross-strait mutual assistance enables freezing of personal and corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Unlicensed Payment Activity, and Sanctions Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PRC parent's Stripe/Paddle accounts to conceal ultimate beneficial ownership, engaging in payment splitting or structuring below AML KYC thresholds, or accepting AI avatar generation payments from sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g., Iran, Russia, North Korea), thereby masking Taiwan-source revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, criminal liability of up to 7 years' imprisonment and fines up to NT$5 million; administrative fines for AML program failures by the paying entity; penalties under the Central Bank Act for unreported cross-border remittances; the concealed Taiwan-source SaaS turnover remains chargeable to 20% corporate income tax, 5% VAT, and the 21% dividend WHT on repatriation, with severe cumulative surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct the structuring or knowingly process sanctioned counterparties face indictment as principals of money laundering; payment-rail settlement accounts may be frozen at the request of the Financial Supervisory Commission; exit bans, asset confiscation, and extradition or cross-strait mutual legal assistance are available.
